title: Appeal of TE John Grady v. Southwest Florida Presbytery
disposition_detail: The SJC affirmed Grady's convictions on all three charges, although not every underlying specification. It sustained procedural errors concerning delayed rulings and telephonic testimony but found them nonprejudicial; rejected the documentary-evidence, prejudice, and questioning claims; and held the BCO 31-10 suspension challenge was not properly before it. It reversed the ruling that refusal to resign violated his submission vow, vacated the indefinite suspension as censure and dissolution of the pastoral relationship, and remanded for reconsideration of censure. The separate administrative suspension remained effective.
first_summary: A minister appealed his conviction and indefinite suspension after refusing Presbytery's direction to resign his pastorate. The SJC upheld the three convictions but held that Presbytery could not convert its authority to dissolve a pastoral relationship into an enforceable resignation directive. It vacated the censure and dissolution of the call and remanded for a new censure determination. His separate administrative suspension remained effective pending further proceedings.
summary: A minister appealed convictions and indefinite suspension arising from conflict over Presbytery's direction that he resign. The SJC upheld all three convictions, finding two procedural errors nonprejudicial and rejecting the other preserved challenges. But Presbytery could not treat its authority to dissolve a pastoral relationship as authority to compel resignation on pain of discipline. The SJC therefore vacated the censure and dissolution of the call and remanded for reconsideration of censure; Grady's separate administrative suspension remained effective.

sources.supports: Issue-level judgments, affirmance and reversal, vacatur, remand, and continuing administrative suspension.
Decisive constitutional distinction between recommending or dissolving a call and compelling resignation through discipline.

evidence_notes.outcomes_and_reasons: Judgments and relief appear at lines 49–80 (printed pp. 165–166); the controlling error and constitutional distinction appear at lines 260–286 (printed pp. 173–174).
evidence_notes.qualifications: The BCO 31-10 challenge was not properly before the SJC, and that administrative suspension continued, lines 149–157 and 286. Two members dissented, but no dissenting opinion is supplied, lines 317–319.
evidence_notes.incorporated_decisions: No decision was incorporated by reference. Cases 94-6 and 2004-9 were cited as similar authority for the firm complaint deadline at line 157.

source_limits: The supplied source contains the adopted opinion and vote record but no text explaining the two dissents.
